title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-07
lineage: [SBD MR > C > D > CD] + [AUD MC > 4C > CD patches]

ai_review.summary: Fair matrix recording with muddy early mix but strong country‑flavored set highlighted by Sawmill, Uncle John’s Band and China Cat > I Know You Rider.
ai_review.review: The composite tape captures a late‑February 1970 Fillmore West show that leans heavily into authentic country material. While the recording suffers from balance problems and early mic‑switch issues – sounding muddy at first – it settles into decent soundboard quality by the second half. Musically the band delivers standout performances of Sawmill, Help on the Way, Uncle John’s Band and a hot China Cat > I Know You Rider sequence, though Good Lovin’ is cut short and some songs feel “blah”.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical set (especially country tunes) while noting consistent recording flaws that keep the overall experience from being great.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part of the show is muddy and suffers from delayed mic switches (boom‑y bass, missing monitor mix). Later tracks achieve clearer soundboard quality, but overall balance problems and occasional cuts remain.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, country‑focused set that starts rough due to sound issues but improves after the first few numbers; the band’s energy stays high throughout, with a strong second half and memorable transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for pedal steel work on country songs and early solo exploration in Uncle John's Band.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as too boomy when the stage mics were not engaged early in the show.
